item.claim: Systolic blood pressure fell numerically more with drug R, but the difference from placebo was not statistically significant (p = 0.247).

item.claim: More patients discontinued because of adverse events on drug R (6.0%) than on placebo (2.3%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports TEAE leading to discontinuation in 18 (6.0%) patients on Drug R 10 mg versus 7 (2.3%) on placebo, matching the claim's percentages and direction of effect.

item.claim: At week 26, drug R reduced HbA1c by 0.94% compared with 0.28% on placebo (difference -0.66%, p < 0.001).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table's Week 26 row reports LS mean changes of -0.94% for drug R and -0.28% for placebo, a difference of -0.66% with p < 0.001, matching every number in the claim.

item.claim: Body weight decreased by 2.1 kg with drug R and 0.6 kg with placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports an LS mean body weight change of -2.1 kg for drug R and -0.6 kg for placebo at week 26, matching the claimed decreases exactly.

item.claim: Drug R reduced HbA1c significantly more than placebo at every visit through week 52.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table lists every visit through Week 52 (Weeks 12, 26, and 52), and at each visit the difference favors Drug R (greater HbA1c reduction than placebo) with p < 0.001, matching the claim of a significant greater reduction at every visit through week 52.

item.claim: Nearly 40% of drug R patients reached HbA1c below 7.0% at week 26, versus about 22% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The source reports 39.9% of drug R patients and 21.8% of placebo patients with HbA1c <7.0% at week 26, matching the claim's 'nearly 40%' and 'about 22%'.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction appeared smaller in patients with eGFR below 60 (difference -0.38%) than in those with eGFR of 60 or above (-0.72%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports a difference of -0.38 (-0.77, 0.01) for eGFR <60 and -0.72 (-0.91, -0.53) for eGFR >=60, matching the claim's numbers and the hedged statement that the reduction 'appeared smaller' in the lower-eGFR subgroup.

item.claim: Fasting plasma glucose fell by 24.3 mg/dL on drug R versus 8.9 mg/dL on placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.quote: Fasting plasma glucose, mg/dL, LS mean change (SE) | -24.3 (2.1) | -8.9 (2.1) | -15.4 (-21.2, -9.6) | <0.001
result.reason: The table reports an LS mean change in fasting plasma glucose at week 26 of -24.3 mg/dL for drug R and -8.9 mg/dL for placebo, matching the claimed values and direction exactly.

item.claim: Shifts in ALT to more than three times the upper limit of normal were rare (0.7% on drug R, 0.3% on placebo).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table shows ALT shifts to >3x ULN in 2 (0.7%) on drug R and 1 (0.3%) on placebo, matching the claim exactly.

item.claim: One patient on drug R and two on placebo died during the study.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports exactly 1 death (0.3%) in the Drug R 10 mg group and 2 deaths (0.7%) in the placebo group, matching the claim.

item.claim: Baseline characteristics were balanced between groups; mean age was 61.2 and 60.8 years and mean HbA1c 8.3% and 8.2%.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports mean age of 61.2 and 60.8 years and mean HbA1c of 8.3% and 8.2% for the two groups, matching the claim exactly, and the near-identical values are consistent with the characterization 'balanced'.

item.claim: The treatment effect on HbA1c was consistent across age subgroups (interaction p = 0.61).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports an age-subgroup interaction p of exactly 0.61 with similar treatment effects in both age groups (-0.69 vs -0.62, overlapping CIs), directly supporting the claim of consistency across age subgroups.

item.claim: Gastrointestinal events were mild and transient.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: severity and duration aren't in the table

result.quote: TEAEs reported in at least 3% of patients in either group, by preferred term (safety population)
result.reason: The table reports only incidence counts and percentages for TEAEs (e.g., Nausea 12.0%, Diarrhoea 8.0%) and contains no data on severity or duration, so it cannot establish that gastrointestinal events were mild and transient.

item.claim: Hypoglycaemia (glucose below 54 mg/dL) was reported in 4.0% of patients on drug R and 1.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports hypoglycaemia (glucose <54 mg/dL) in 12 (4.0%) of Drug R patients and 3 (1.0%) of placebo patients, exactly matching the claim.

item.claim: Drug R is safe in patients with renal impairment.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Overview of treatment-emergent adverse events (safety population)
result.reason: The cited table is an overview of TEAEs in the general safety population and contains no data on patients with renal impairment, so it cannot support a safety claim specific to that population.

item.claim: Drug R did not increase the risk of hypoglycaemia.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table shows hypoglycaemia occurred in 4.0% of Drug R patients versus 1.0% of placebo patients, a four-fold higher rate in the Drug R group, which contradicts the claim that Drug R did not increase hypoglycaemia risk.

item.claim: Nausea was the most common adverse event with drug R, reported by 12.0% of patients versus 4.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table shows nausea at 12.0% (36/300) with drug R versus 4.0% (12/298) with placebo, and it is the highest percentage in the drug R column, with all other listed events lower and unlisted events below the 3% table threshold.

item.claim: Older patients (65 years and above) derived a significantly smaller benefit than younger patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table shows an age-by-treatment interaction p-value of 0.61, so the numerically smaller HbA1c benefit in patients >=65 years (-0.62 vs -0.69) is not statistically significant, contradicting the claim of a 'significantly smaller benefit'.

item.claim: In patients with eGFR below 60, drug R significantly reduced HbA1c versus placebo (difference -0.38%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The point estimate of -0.38 matches, but the 95% CI (-0.77, 0.01) crosses zero, so the source does not support the claim of a statistically significant reduction.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction with drug R increased steadily through week 52.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Week 26, LS mean change (SE) | -0.94 (0.06) ... Week 52, LS mean change (SE) | -0.81 (0.07)
result.reason: The HbA1c reduction with drug R increased from week 12 (-0.72) to week 26 (-0.94) but then declined at week 52 (-0.81), so it did not increase steadily through week 52.

item.claim: Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates in the two groups (7.0% and 6.4%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports serious TEAEs in 21/300 (7.0%) of the Drug R 10 mg group and 19/298 (6.4%) of the placebo group, matching the claimed rates, and the 0.6 percentage-point difference is consistent with the characterization 'similar'.

item.claim: The HbA1c benefit of drug R was consistent across renal function subgroups.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table shows a significant treatment-by-renal-function interaction (p = 0.04) and a smaller, non-significant effect in the eGFR <60 subgroup (-0.38, 95% CI -0.77 to 0.01, crossing zero) versus eGFR >=60 (-0.72), contradicting the claim of a consistent benefit across renal function subgroups.

item.claim: Drug R was well tolerated, with an adverse event profile similar to placebo.

item.claim: The maximal HbA1c reduction was reached by week 12.

item.claim: Weight loss with drug R was driven by its gastrointestinal effects.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table confirms greater weight loss with drug R versus placebo at week 26, but it contains no data on gastrointestinal effects or any mechanism, so it cannot establish that the weight loss was driven by GI effects.

item.claim: Drug R tripled the proportion of patients reaching HbA1c below 7.0%.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The source shows the proportion reaching HbA1c <7.0% rose from 21.8% (placebo) to 39.9% (Drug R), roughly a 1.8-fold increase (OR 2.41), not a tripling as the claim states.

item.claim: Drug R also lowered systolic blood pressure compared with placebo.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table shows no statistically significant difference in systolic BP between Drug R and placebo (difference -1.3, 95% CI -3.5 to 0.9, p=0.247), so the source does not support the claim that Drug R lowered systolic BP versus placebo.

result.reason: The table reports only the incidence of urinary tract infection as a treatment-emergent adverse event (5.0% with Drug R vs 4.7% with placebo) and does not establish that Drug R caused the infections, so the claim's causal language goes beyond the source.

item.claim: Any adverse event was reported by 57.0% of drug R patients and 61.0% of placebo patients.

item.claim: Haematocrit decreased with drug R.
item.label: not_supported
